facts.value: Builds an output matrix from a joint-relative matrix and its ancestor chain. For each subject column, uses reciprocal magnitude above 1e-10 and otherwise the magnitude itself, then multiplies by the corresponding current joint-matrix column length. For ancestors, reciprocal normalization occurs above 1e-5; tiny columns instead multiply by their magnitude. Concatenates ancestor transforms into out. This is not guaranteed orthonormal or scale-free.
facts.rationale: Tiny columns are multiplied by their magnitude rather than normalized; preserved subject scale prevents universal orthonormality.

facts.value: Returns when the computed f32 sum dir.x*dir.x + dir.y*dir.y + dir.z*dir.z equals zero, including possible underflow from tiny nonzero components. Otherwise sets up the joint matrix and computes its Z-column magnitude. A nonzero computed magnitude yields atan2(-dir.x * mtx[2][2]/magnitude,dir.y). Tests angle>max_angle first, assigning max_angle, then tests angle<-min_angle, assigning -min_angle. Updates Euler Z or composes a quaternion Z rotation, marks dirty in the quaternion branch and sets up the matrix again. dir.z only affects the squared-sum guard; the fifth argument is unused.
facts.rationale: State exact numeric operations and mutable state without stronger geometric guarantees.

facts.value: A computed squared-direction sum equal to zero returns before matrix setup. A sum unequal to zero reaches HSD_JObjSetupMatrix even if the later computed Z-column magnitude is zero, in which case rotation adjustment is skipped. Upper then lower clamp tests are sequential. If -min_angle>max_angle, the second test can replace the upper-clamped value with -min_angle and exceed max_angle. Bounds ordering and NaN are not validated.
facts.rationale: Matrix setup can occur before zero-column rejection; no-transform-change wording was too broad.

facts.value: Writes projected positions and measured lengths in place. With S=10*(len0+len1)/11 and d=distance(pos0,pos4), d>S replaces d by 11*S/10 - S^11/(10*d^10). Two cosine quotients are clamped by comparisons before acos. If pi-acos2 is below 0.1745329201221466, the formula blends from 2.9670597334676465 toward acos2 using abs(pi-acos2)/0.1745329201221466. No zero-denominator or NaN guard is present.
facts.rationale: Preserve exact reach and near-extension formula without claiming a universal angle floor.
